cited.quote: Under this scheme, the Self Help Groups exclusively of tribal women can avail assistance
Adi Dravidar women Self Help Groups, Men Self Help Groups, both Women and Men Self Help Groups

rationale: C1-C4 are policy notes describing TAHDCO economic assistance to SHGs including women's groups, but they report a pre-existing scheme and amounts 'allocated' or 'to be provided'. No extract shows a GO, launch or other official step dated after the government took office. Status not_started; the scheme appears to be ongoing activity only.
C1-C3 concern salt pan land lease rent and royalty, C4 Anganwadi training and C5 income-tax deductions. None is about a rainy season maintenance allowance for salt pan workers.
C1 and C3 cover Amma Unavagam and Amma Kudineer, C2 health schemes, C4 and C5 departmental exam syllabi on banking. No extract mentions an Amma Banking Card or a financial-services card with banks.

cited.quote: The development works have commenced in September 2018 and expected completion by October – 2020.
Presently, Cuddalore Port is being developed as Deep water, all weather port at a cost of Rs.135 crore

rationale: Directional commitment. C2 and C3 show a dedicated project developing Cuddalore Port as a deep water port (Rs.135 crore, Sagarmala/Coastal Berth Scheme), with works commenced in September 2018 (C3). That is a dedicated official measure beyond preparation. C1 is only a plan statement.

cited.quote: accord administrative sanction for provision of free internet facility in 366 Government Higher Secondary Schools
The scheme of distribution of Laptop computer to students will continue to be implemented during the current year 2016-17

rationale: C1-C3 describe laptop distribution but no internet connection with the laptops. C5 sanctions free internet in 366 government higher secondary schools, which is a related step for schools, not an internet connection given with students' laptops. No official step for the commitment itself.

cited.quote: Project Proposal of Department of Tamil Nadu Dr. J.Jayalalitha Fisheries University - Administrative and Financial Sanction
Establishment of Fisheries Training Institute at Mandapam, Ramanathapuram District – Rs.450 lakh.

rationale: C5 is a GO (16.07.2018) giving administrative and financial sanction for the Fisheries University's project proposals (technology park, referral laboratory). C2 lists projects carried out in 2018-19, including a Fisheries Training Institute and para-professional institute. C1 covers works from 2015-16, before the government took office. 'Improve' has no defined target, so these steps count as fulfilment.
The commitment ('Implement this scheme') does not name the scheme. None of C1-C5 can be identified as being about it.

cited.quote: has ordered for the enhancement of the grant given for the renovation of temples
In the year 2016-2017 Hon’ble Former Chief Minister Puratchi Thalaivi Amma ordered for an enhancement of this assistance to Rs.1,00,000/- each.

rationale: C4 (dated 2016-09-29) reports an order raising the renovation grant for temples in Adi Dravida and Tribal habitations from Rs.50,000 to one lakh rupees from the current financial year 2016-2017. C5 confirms the enhancement to Rs.1,00,000 each and Rs.10.19 crore disbursed to 1019 temples in 2017-18.

cited.quote: Loan issued to the small and marginal farmers by the Cooperative Banks as on 31.3.2016 be waived.
12,02,075 farmers have been benefitted to the tune of Rs.5318.73 crore
Guidelines to Co-operative Institutions on the waiver of Agricultural Loans

rationale: C3 is G.O.(Ms) No.50 dated 23.05.2016 ordering the waiver of outstanding crop, medium-term and long-term loans of small and marginal farmers with cooperative banks. C1 and C2 issue the guidelines (28.6.2016). C4 reports 12,02,075 farmers benefited (Rs.5318.73 crore). Scope matches the promise.

cited.quote: inland fisheries policy for Tamil Nadu has been framed and is under the consideration of the Government
Establishment of Inland Fish Landing Centres in Thirumoorthy and Amaravathy Reservoirs

rationale: Directional. C1 says an inland fisheries policy has been framed and is under the Government's consideration, which is a preparatory step. C4 is a GO on inland fish landing centres (landing infrastructure, not production). C2 and C3 are policy-note descriptions of continuing activity. No order giving priority to inland fish production is shown.

cited.quote: inland fisheries policy for Tamil Nadu has been framed and is under the consideration of the Government
set a goal to enhance the inland fish production three fold from the present level of production

rationale: Directional. C1 reports a draft inland fisheries policy under consideration plus initiatives described only in a policy note. C3 states a goal. C4's GO sanctions fisheries projects (ice boxes, outboard motors, brackish water mapping), not inland production. C5 concerns landing centres. Only a preparatory step for a dedicated inland-production scheme is shown.

cited.quote: For Pongal 2017, 160.21 lakh Sarees and 159.98 lakh Dhoties were produced and supplied to Revenue Department
This scheme is being implemented for distribution of Sarees and Dhoties to the poor people living in rural and urban areas

rationale: The promise is to continue the free dhoti and saree scheme. C2 reports sarees and dhotis produced and supplied for Pongal 2017, and C1 reports supply for Pongal 2018, so the scheme was carried on. C3 is a budget provision only. C4 and C5 concern Anganwadi uniform sarees.

cited.quote: By year 2023, make the Government services accessible online from anywhere or nearby Common Service Delivery outlets
The following facilities / services are available in the website https://ctd.tn.gov.in, for the mercantile public

rationale: C4 is a GO (16.11.2017) approving the e-Governance Policy, whose vision is all government services online by 2023. That is an official step, not delivery. C2 shows online services for one department only. No extract shows all government services available through the website.

cited.quote: TANTRANSCO is consistently planning and executing additional transmission infrastructure at voltage levels of 110 kV and above
During the year 2019-20 (as on 31.01.2020), 80 nos. 33 kV substations, 5,718 kms of LT lines

rationale: Directional. C1 and C3 are policy notes describing continuing transmission and distribution network expansion by the utilities. No new GO, scheme or programme dedicated to strengthening the grid is shown. C2, C4 and C5 cover solar, free electricity and building rules.

cited.quote: Detailed Project Report was prepared by NABARD Consultancy Services (NABCONS) and administrative sanction was issued on 21.06.2016.
Government of Tamil Nadu is establishing a network of primary processing centres to connect farm gates with the terminal markets/food processing

rationale: C1 reports administrative sanction issued on 21.06.2016 for the supply chain management project, which creates post-harvest infrastructure and backward and forward linkages for fruits and vegetables. C3 (Food Processing Policy GO, 2018) confirms the network of primary processing centres being established. The order was issued after the government took office.

cited.quote: transforming them into Farmer Producer Organizations through Forward and Backward Linkages as prescribed in the Guidelines annexed to this order
the Government have enacted Tamil Nadu Agricultural Produce & Livestock Contract Farming and Services (Promotion and Facilitation) Act, 2019

rationale: C4 is a GO (29.06.2017) sanctioning Rs.100 crore for 2000 Farmer Producer Groups, to become FPOs with forward and backward market linkages. C2 reports the Contract Farming Act, 2019, which gives farmers pre-agreed prices. Together they connect farmers to demand and better prices. C1 and C3 are general policy-note descriptions.
The commitment ('Continuously implement these schemes') does not say which schemes. None of C1-C5 can be tied to it.

cited.quote: The scheme was inaugurated by the Hon’ble Prime Minister of India in the presence of the Hon’ble Chief Minister on 24.02.2018
A maximum subsidy of 50% of the cost of the vehicle or Rs.25,000, whichever is less, is provided to purchase a two wheeler.

rationale: C1 and C3 describe the Amma Two Wheeler Scheme for working women, implemented from 2017-18 and launched on 24.02.2018 (C1), with 1,12,972 beneficiaries. C2 gives the subsidy: 50% of vehicle cost or Rs.25,000, whichever is less, for mopeds/scooters. This matches the promise. C4 and C5 concern EV policy.

cited.quote: The Government of Tamil Nadu on 30.11.2018 filed a Miscellaneous Application in the Supreme Court

rationale: C5: the state objected to the Mekedatu dam, filed a Supreme Court application (30.11.2018) and a contempt petition, and the CM wrote to the PM (24.06.2019). Despite this, the Central Water Commission allowed Karnataka to prepare the DPR, and the cases are pending. The state acted, but prevention depended on the Union and the courts. C1-C4 report steps from before the government took office.

cited.quote: The Government have increased the unemployment assistance by 100 % with effect from February, 2017.
Rs.300/- for SSLC passed, Rs.400/- for HSC passed and Rs.600/- for the graduates

rationale: C1 shows unemployment assistance doubled from February 2017: SSLC passed Rs.300, HSC Rs.400, graduates Rs.600. These are exactly the promised amounts, and C3 confirms them. C2 concerns differently abled persons. C4 and C5 concern UYEGP subsidies.
